instruction.text: Look at the line graph showing a narrowboat journey and answer the questions.

atoms.a: Between which two hours was Charlie moving the fastest?
atoms.b: He was moving the fastest between hour <mat><gap>0 1</gap></mat> and hour <mat><gap>1 0</gap></mat>.

atoms.a: How far had Charlie travelled after 3 hours?
What was the total amount of time that Charlie was not moving?
Charlie was stationary twice during his journey: to have lunch in a pub and to use a lock. Which stop was most likely for lunch?

text.text: A lock is a system of gates that let water in and out of a confined space. This means the water level can rise and fall which allows canal boats to travel up and down hills.

atoms.b: Charlie most likely had lunch at stop ((++1 2)).

atoms.a: Emma spent more time stationary than moving. True or false?
Was Emma moving faster between hours 3 and 4 or 4 and 4.5?

atoms.a: How many kilometres had Emma travelled after 3.5 hours?
atoms.sound: How many kilometres had Emma travelled after 3 and a half hours?

instruction.text: Look at the line graph showing a half-marathon and answer the questions.

atoms.a: How many miles did Andrew cover during the fastest section?

hint.text: What other parts of the line have the same steepness? Andrew also ran these parts at 4 miles per hour.
